content:
Over the years, Apple has continued to add more customization options to iOS. iOS 16 brought back full lock screen personalization, then iOS 18 introduced icon tinting, iOS 26 introduced translucent icons, and iOS 27 brings full-screen Liquid Glass sliders.

It is great that iPhone personalization continues to expand. Now that you can tint your home screen icons — why not extend that functionality across the entire operating system?

iOS 27 hasn't been released yet, so thinking about what Apple might do with its next software version is perhaps getting ahead of myself. Even so, I think adding themed application color schemes beyond light and dark mode is a logical next step.

Basically, I want to replicate Material You's design on iOS — but based on icon color instead of wallpaper — though Apple should also offer the wallpaper-based option. Apple last year debuted an option that lets icons match the color of your MagSafe case, which would also fit right in if this theming system was added.

It's worth noting that Apple earlier this year at WWDC already introduced color theming for its integrated development environment, Xcode. There are a ton of great options there — why not bring that fun to the iPhone? At this point, even the Mac allows you to set system-wide tints for third-party apps.

Conclusion

Overall, I just think color theming on iOS would look great, and would be another step toward giving users more customization.

What do you think about adding color theming to iOS and iPadOS? Let us know in the comments.
